decisions.reason: Define-XML ADQSADAS.EFFFL names ADSL.FASFL, which is absent from the retained ADSL dataset; the implemented ADSL.EFFFL is a different named source.

Define-XML ADQSADAS.CHG states the unqualified AVAL - BASE that the literal probe runs, giving the baseline zero-versus-missing differences, and SAP pages 29 and 14 justify the CHG__POSTBASELINE reading that reproduces the reference. CHG__PROGRAM is labelled as a program reading, and adadas.r L162-L165 do compute final CHG only where ABLFL is missing, so it shows how the reference was computed rather than serving as documentation.

The differing records are added ACTOT LOCF recipients whose QSSEQ traces a baseline donor, rather than collected baseline records governed by the QS.QSBLFL copy in ADQSADAS.ABLFL. SAP page-10 distinguishes missing postbaseline recipients from baseline values, so the donor baseline flag does not establish that the recipient is baseline.

Define-XML ADQSADAS.STUDYID and data guide page-4 name ADSL as the source, while the global derivation and all four QS row templates obtain the identifier from QS. The keyed ADSL input supplies other columns but does not supply this identifier.

Define-XML ADQSADAS.USUBJID and data guide page-4 name ADSL as the source, while the global derivation and all four QS row templates obtain the identifier from QS. No intermediate in that path returns ADSL.USUBJID.

SAP page-11 specifies visit date minus randomization date, while obs uses the TRTSDT-relative study_day operation documented in ADQSADAS.ADY, including its on-or-after increment. The visit-3 sources identify the reference visit but do not make these two arithmetic definitions equal.

SAP page-11 assigns Week 24 only above day 140, whereas the final obs branch accepts every remaining input, including missing ADY. The original PDF confirms the earlier baseline boundary is <=1, which does not repair this unconditional fallback.

The obs rule copies QS.VISIT, and locf8, locf16 and locf24 copy _SRC_VISIT from DONOR8, DONOR16 and DONOR24, each sourced from SELF observations. Every path therefore resolves to the QS.VISIT source named in ADQSADAS.VISIT; donor selection is a separate question.

The obs rule copies QS.VISITNUM, and every LOCF template obtains _SRC_VISITNUM through its DONOR intermediate from SELF observations. These transitive paths preserve the QS.VISITNUM source stated in ADQSADAS.VISITNUM.

SAP page-10 limits LOCF to missing postbaseline efficacy values, but obs assigns _CARRIED_AVAL to every ACTOT row. That branch can replace an observed score and has no missing-score or postbaseline condition.

SAP page-11 selects the prior assessment in an equidistant pair, while obs sorts ascending AWTARGET-ADY after absolute distance. That order places the later assessment first and changes the selected score carried forward.

Native SDTM Define-XML QS.QSSTRESN points to COMPMETHOD.QSAD_QSSTRESN, which states that ADAS total scores were derived as described in the SAP, so reading the submitted ACTOT total is a documented upstream computation. The empty SDTM section export omits that source context; the separate unconditional carry and selection differences do not show that the item-sum adjustment itself was replaced.

Native SDTM Define-XML QS.QSBLFL sets Y for VISIT=BASELINE, and the visit codelist identifies that visit as 3, supplying the condition cited in ADQSADAS.BASE. On those baseline observations the selected AVAL path returns the raw QS score, so ONLY(AVAL) under ABLFL=Y is the same baseline computation rather than a different source rule.

ADQSADAS.BASE and ADQSADAS.ABLFL identify baseline using QS.QSBLFL, and obs preserves that flag while the added postbaseline LOCF rows leave it blank. The complementary ABLFL condition expresses the post-baseline applicability stated on SAP page-29; the finding does not establish an additional documentary definition of post-baseline status.

ADQSADAS.CHG is AVAL-BASE only when ABLFL is not Y, so substitution into the PCHG formula preserves both the arithmetic and its baseline missingness. The BASE<>0 guard implements the undefined quotient as missing and does not add a clinical condition to 100*(CHG/BASE).

The obs flag copies the Y-versus-blank meaning of QS.QSBLFL, and the added LOCF rows are postbaseline recipients even when their metadata donor is baseline. ADQSADAS.ABLFL and SAP page-10 do not require propagating a donor baseline flag onto those synthetic target visits.

SAP page-11 requires the pre-target assessment for equidistant observations, whereas ascending AWTARGET-ADY in obs prefers the later observation. The absolute-distance primary sort does not remove this opposite tie preference.

Data guide page-6 defines DTYPE by whether AVAL was imputed using LOCF, while obs infers that event from numeric inequality or a newly nonmissing score. The _CARRIED_AVAL path can use LOCF without that inequality, so the event definition and the implemented test are different.

SAP page-10 allows imputation of missing postbaseline efficacy values, but the obs DTYPE condition also marks changed nonmissing ACTOT scores and has no postbaseline guard. The original source-value comparison does not impose either documented restriction.

Data guide page-6 limits LOCF candidates to records used for analysis (ANL01FL='Y'), but DONOR8, DONOR16 and DONOR24 rank every ACTOT record at or below the target visit with no ANL01FL condition, and locf8, locf16 and locf24 copy that donor's QSSEQ. An added LOCF row can therefore carry the sequence of an unselected observation; the native ADQSADAS.QSSEQ.ACTOT missing-sequence comment is a further difference, not a counterpart that matches DONOR8.

SAP pages 9 and 11 with Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT complete the windows for collected assessments, but SAP pages 10 and 14 and data guide page-6 do not say which records are created LOCF recipients or how their AVISIT is assigned while donor ADT is kept. adadas.r L117-L139 show the later reimplementation taking the recipient visit from an expected-visit table, an implementation choice that does not fill the documentation gap.

ADQSADAS.ADT states SAS date conversion from QS.QSDTC, and native QS.QSDTC identifies the corresponding SV visit date, but neither states first-day completion of partial dates. The first-of-month statement on data guide page-5 is specific to adverse events.

Native ADQSADAS.AVAL.ACITM01 through ACITM14 explicitly match QSTESTCD=PARAMCD, and the native QS and ADaM code metadata identify the ACTOT total. These retained value-level source associations support the observed code identity even though the scalar PARAMCD section omits them.

Native ADQSADAS.DTYPE value-level metadata reserves the LOCF definition for ACTOT and assigns null to the item parameters, while SAP pages 10 and 14 describe LOCF for the total endpoint. The ACTOT assignment in locf8 and the later templates expresses that parameter scope; row-emission eligibility is a separate clause.

Native Define-XML ADQSADAS.AVAL.ACITM01-ACITM14 (QS.QSSTRESN where QSTESTCD=PARAMCD) and ADQSADAS.AVAL.ACTOT, with the PARAMCD codelist and the ACTOT-only ADQSADAS.DTYPE.ACTOT rule, identify the item and total codes and the LOCF total scope. The added adadas.r L54-L57 and L117-L139 are a later implementation and do not change that the retained documents supply the rule, whose omission from the scalar sections is an adapter limit.

SAP pages 10-11 and data guide page-6 state only that LOCF carries targeted assessments forward, and SAP Appendix 1 on pages 45-47 adds scoring and missing-item rules; none states the DONOR8 ranking by descending AVISITN, ADY and QSSEQ with keep first. DONOR16 and DONOR24 repeat this undocumented donor order and QSSEQ tie-break.

SAP page-10 triggers LOCF from missing postbaseline efficacy values, but does not state the locf8 test for a null _HIT and nonnull donor sequence. The same sequence-presence emission test in locf16 and locf24 is not a documented score-missingness rule.

Native ADQSADAS.AVAL value-level rules supply the item copies and the SAP-derived total, but SAP pages 10-11 and data guide page-6 do not complete the same-day targeted-assessment tie or the added-recipient eligibility needed for the carried value. adadas.r L51, L76 and L125-L139 show the reimplementation copying QSSTRESN and creating LOCF records, which is how the reference was computed, not a documented rule.

ADQSADAS.ANL01FL and data guide page-6 identify selected observed assessments and records used for analysis, but do not explicitly assign Y to every emitted LOCF row. SAP pages 10-11 do not supply the complete eligibility rule for those additional flagged records.

SAP page-11 resolves equidistant assessments on opposite sides of the target but not repeated assessments on the same closest day, and Define-XML ADQSADAS.ANL01FL and data guide page-6 do not state that every added LOCF record is flagged Y. adadas.r L102-L113 and L141 show the reimplementation's ordering and its Y on created records, which are implementation choices rather than documentation.

Native ADQSADAS.DTYPE value-level metadata gives item nulls and the ACTOT LOCF meaning, but SAP pages 10-11 and data guide page-6 leave recipient eligibility and selected-assessment ties incomplete, so the imputation event cannot be reconstructed independently. adadas.r L125-L139 show DTYPE set on created ACTOT records in the reimplementation, which does not supply the missing documented rule.

Define-XML ADQSADAS.AWRANGE points to the four SAP page-11 intervals, and the finding's own note says the original PDF baseline cell is <=1, so the lost underline is a text-extraction limit, not a missing source, condition or computation. The <=1 string in adadas.r L83-L89 is a later implementation choice and is not evidence of what the SAP states.

SAP page-11 gives baseline an unbounded lower interval, so the null Baseline entry represents the absence of a finite beginning day under ADQSADAS.AWLO. It introduces no extra window condition or computation requiring a separate clinical rule.

Define-XML ADQSADAS.AWLO and SAP page-11 give every finite window start and no finite lower endpoint for Baseline, and storing that nonexistent value as missing is ordinary numeric semantics, not an unstated rule. adadas.r L83-L89 and L142-L147 show the same missing value in the reimplementation but are not documentation.
SAP page-11 defines Week 24 as above day 140 with no finite upper endpoint. The missing Week 24 entry in AWHI represents that open endpoint rather than adding an undocumented derivation clause.

Define-XML ADQSADAS.AWHI and SAP page-11 give the finite window ends, with Baseline ending at day 1 and no finite end for Week 24, so a missing Week 24 value is the ordinary encoding of an open endpoint. adadas.r L83-L89 and L142-L147 show the reimplementation using the same encoding and do not serve as documentation.

Native Define-XML ADQSADAS.QSSEQ.ACITM01-ACITM14 copy QS.QSSEQ, and ADQSADAS.QSSEQ.ACTOT sets postbaseline sequence missing and takes QS.QSSEQ from the baseline ACTOT record, which completes the rule; its absence from the scalar section is an adapter limit. adadas.r L136, where the reimplementation carries donor QSSEQ onto created records, shows how that program computes the value and does not make the documentation incomplete.

SAP page-9 anchors randomization at Visit 3, but adqsadas.yaml obs uses ADSL.TRTSDT from adsl-yamaa.parquet. The declared upstream adsl.yaml derives that date from EX_MINDTC at lines 384-398, leaving no executable Visit-3 selection in this window-source chain.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT requires the Visit-3 SV.SVSTDTC source, while adqsadas.yaml imports the maintained ADSL output and its upstream TRTSDT uses MIN(EX.EXSTDTC). The matching source comment at adsl.yaml line 407 does not implement the missing SV selection.

missed.quote:
The datasets include only subjects who were enrolled in the study. Subjects who failed screening 
criteria were not included in analysis datasets.
missed.reason: The enrolled-subject restriction governs the observed row population and the subjects eligible for its added LOCF rows, but no claim cites this record-selection statement.
